title: NOT_SENT is accepted for an already-DISPATCHED/resent submit: the leg is finalised, its reservation is freed and a new ENTRY CID is allowed after a timeout
requirement: NG-HIST-004 (no new ID after timeout/crash), NG-DB-005, AC-56, AC-17
original_scenario: The entry submit times out, so the store records UNKNOWN and the leg is SUBMIT_UNKNOWN with its reservation held. The engine then calls mark_dispatching(resend_same_cid=True), which clears outcome to NULL and sets attempts=2. On the resend, the port's local pre-validation fails (for example the runtime minimum changed) and returns NOT_SENT. record_transport_result maps this to REJECTED_UNSENT, a final state, and releases the reservation. _check_single_physical_entry then allows ENTRY revision 1 with a new CID. The first attempt may still be live or filled on the venue, so exposure is doubled under a new CID. If the first attempt then fills, _apply_trade reports it as EVIDENCE_FOR_UNDISPATCHED_INTENT and the fill is never credited. The same happens after a restart: a DISPATCHED row left by the dead process accepts NOT_SENT.
verifier_residual: Reachable only through a direct store call. The engine records NOT_SENT only for PENDING rows (engine.py:1754-1766 _close_open_outbox, 2393-2399 pre-send happens before mark_dispatching, 2417-2429 _withdraw/_pending_submit_outbox), so the integrated engine does not hit it today. Any future caller that treats a dead process's DISPATCHED row as unsent would free the reservation and allow a new ENTRY CID.
verifier_evidence: The resend scenario is fixed: attempts>1 (store.py:3031) and an earlier non-NOT_SENT attempt (store.py:3033-3037) both keep the leg SUBMIT_UNKNOWN and the reservation. Covered by ::test_review4_release_outcome_on_a_resend_keeps_unknown_and_reservation (passes; mutation test_mut_b01_release_blocker_none makes it fail). The restart variant named in the finding is still reachable at the store API. Probe scratchpad/verify/test_probe_b.py::test_probe_b09_restart_dispatched_row_not_sent: intent, then mark_dispatching commits, then a crash before transport, then reopen, then record_transport_result(NOT_SENT) on the DISPATCHED row (attempts==1). Result: leg=REJECTED_UNSENT, reservations=[] (released). No owner or process token ties NOT_SENT to the process that dispatched the row, and no repo test covers this case (test_ac16_crash_after_dispatch_mark_is_ambiguous_not_absent does not try NOT_SENT).

title: The UI never shows a persistence failure: the banner needs a snapshot that cannot be committed, so the UI only shows STALE while CLI status shows the error
requirement: NG-DB-004 / AC-55 (the UI shows the persistence failure), §11 (CLI status and UI show the same state)
original_scenario: The disk fills or the database becomes read-only. Engine.tick catches PersistenceError and never commits a snapshot while the store is degraded (engine.py:612-616, 625-627). So summary.persistence_error is never present in a committed snapshot and the persistence banner never appears. The web shows the last state (for example NORMAL) as current for up to stale_after_s, then «Нет свежих данных». The demo host holds the engine in-process, but host.status() does not expose engine.persistence_error, and the UI does not render `host`. The CLI status (executor.py:304 local_error) does print «LOCAL ERROR (not committed): SQLITE_FULL».
verifier_residual: Attach mode on a full or read-only filesystem, the headline scenario, still shows no persistence banner. A variant with a writable directory (for example a DB locked only through SQLite) is covered.
verifier_evidence: The in-process host is fixed. host.py:77-90 exposes engine persistence_error and fatal_reason, and views.health_view (views.py:250-271) turns them into the «не зафиксировано» banner. Covered by test_ngweb_health.py::test_in_process_host_reports_engine_persistence_error. Attach mode uses the engine sidecar <db>.health.json (engine.py:746-763; runtime.py:212-242). The engine writes the file only when its status changes, into the same directory as the DB, so the first tick leaves a 'healthy' file behind. Probe scratchpad/verify/probe_e03_sidecar.py ran a real Harness, applied FaultHooks.simulate_disk_full and made the data directory read-only to model a full or read-only filesystem. Result: engine.persistence_error='...SQLITE_FULL...', every sidecar write failed with 'could not be written', and the file still held persistence_error=null from the first tick. health_view then returned known=True, banner=None next to a stale snapshot. The UI therefore shows only STALE, which is the original failure mode. The stale-snapshot «неизвестно» fallback fires only when the file is missing or unreadable, not when it is outdated. The tests (test_ngweb_health.py::test_attach_health_file_error_shown_next_to_stale; engine test_w3_health_sidecar_*) cover only a hand-written error file, or disk-full on SQLite while the sidecar stays writable.

title: Attach mode: Start preview and risk/baseline confirmation come from a separate --config YAML and are never checked against the config the engine actually runs
requirement: NG-UI-002 (first live start needs a separate explicit confirmation of B and risk, based on a preview of the real grid); NG-UI-001 (versioned committed snapshot); NG-UI-003 (Start returns the existing engine identity)
original_scenario: The engine runs in the Hummingbot executor from the controller YAML with Q=20 and caps 2000. The web is started with --attach-db and a stale or different grid.yml (Q=10, caps 1000, other grid_id). /api/preview shows P_min/P_max [-330,+220], gross 550/1000 and no errors. The operator types B and ticks the risk box, and POST start returns 202. The engine applies START without looking at preview_id or B (engine.py:722-734). CONFIRM_BASELINE only compares B, so the engine then trades a grid with twice the exposure the operator confirmed. /api/state and the 409 engine_already_running responses also report the web YAML's grid_id instead of the engine's. Reproduced with a scratch script: snapshot summary had grid_id=engine-real-grid, order_amount_base=20 and caps 2000. The preview showed Q=10, cap 1000, errors []. Start returned 202, and identity came back as {'grid_id': 'web-yaml-grid'}.
verifier_residual: The engine trades a grid whose preview and risk were never acknowledged, whenever the config changes between an applied START and CONFIRM_BASELINE. Fix: record the config fingerprint at START and reset or refuse started/CONFIRM_BASELINE on a mismatch, or have the web refuse confirm when the applied START's preview material differs from the current engine_config.
verifier_evidence: The literal scenario is fixed. The web no longer reads a separate YAML. Preview, preview_id, the B check and engine_identity all come from the snapshot's engine_config (runtime.py:253-269), and the store rejects stale revisions at enqueue and at claim (store.py:3943-3956). Covered by test_ngweb_attach.py::test_attach_preview_identity_and_baseline_come_from_engine_config, and my real-engine probe matched. A variant is still reachable, because the engine never binds the acknowledged START to the config it runs. engine.py:845-883 validates only the format of preview_id and stores meta.start_preview_id without ever comparing it. meta.started persists across restarts, and a pre-bootstrap config change is accepted. Probe scratchpad/verify/probe_e_restart_cfg.py: START applied for a Q=10 config, restart with Q=20 and caps of 2000 before bootstrap, and the snapshot still says started=True. Web confirm_baseline is then allowed (commands.py:245 checks only engine_started), and CONFIRM_BASELINE with B=0 was APPLIED and bootstrapped the Q=20 grid. The operator's risk acknowledgement covered a different grid.

title: A history conflict or ledger-invariant freeze on one cell withholds every cell's TP obligations and skips the outside-bounds entry cancels
requirement: NG-OPS-001 (pause keeps servicing confirmed TP obligations; a fill gap or unknown blocks only new exposure of the affected cell), NG-HIST-002 (a key with a different payload -> history conflict and pause), NG-RISK-003 (does not abandon TP obligations), NG-OPS-002 (entries are cancel-requested outside bounds)
original_scenario: The venue serves one contradictory trade row for cell A (an overfill on A's CID). The store opens an OVERFILL conflict, tp_blockers becomes ['HISTORY_CONFLICT'] and _act returns early. Cell B is unrelated: its entry fully fills, history is complete and exact, E = 10, and venue net is +10. B still gets no TP for 60 s, and none until an operator runs ack_history_conflict. When the book then leaves the range, no OUTSIDE_BOUNDS cancel is sent: 0 cancels, 9 entries stay live. Any StoreError or LedgerError raised anywhere in a tick behaves the same way, for example an active-orders row that contradicts a leg, because it latches FREEZE_INVARIANT, which is in _FREEZES_BLOCKING_TP.
verifier_residual: A refusal that recurs every tick withholds every cell's TPs and every outside-bounds or risk-reducing cancel until an operator acts, which is the finding's own example. Any persistent StoreError or LedgerError raised in `_scan_history`, `_reconcile_active`, `_settle` or `_detect_drift` does the same. No test pins the recurring case.
verifier_evidence: Checked at HEAD 203e31370. engine.py:124 now blocks TPs engine-wide only for CID_ALLOCATION and CONFIG_MISMATCH. engine.py:1928-1958 (`_scoped_tp_blocks`) limits HISTORY_CONFLICT and LEDGER_INVARIANT blocking to the affected cells, applied at engine.py:2084-2086. engine.py:2153-2158 plus 2123-2135 keep risk-reducing cancels (OUTSIDE_BOUNDS, cancel retries, unsent cancels) flowing while TPs are blocked. Tests test_ng_engine_review1.py::test_r02_one_cells_history_conflict_does_not_withhold_other_cells_tps_or_risk_cancels and ::test_r02_ledger_invariant_freeze_keeps_tps_of_exact_cells_and_outside_bounds_cancels pass. Both runtime mutations make them fail: putting LEDGER_INVARIANT back in `_FREEZES_BLOCKING_TP`, and a global HISTORY_CONFLICT TP blocker. The finding's own example still reproduces, though. Probe scratchpad/verify/test_probe_d102.py makes the active-orders row of cell A's entry contradict its leg (initial_base_amount 11 != 10). `record_order_evidence` then raises InvalidTransitionError in `_reconcile_active` (engine.py:1663) on every tick. The tick is caught at engine.py:737-743 before `_act` (engine.py:729), which never runs: `_reload` resets `_active_reconciled_at`, so the same row raises again. Result: cell B's 10 fill was committed but B had no TP after 15 ticks, and the outside-bounds move gave 0 cancels over 8 ticks, with the engine FROZEN and STORE_REFUSED every tick. r02 only covers a one-time refusal (refuse_once).

title: A WS trade signal arriving after its row is already committed creates a permanent phantom history lag
requirement: AC-13 (lag visible in status; history lag measured separately from the WS event), NG-HIST-001, AC-09 (reordered events)
original_scenario: A fill's trade row is committed by a scan first. Later the private-stream or connector fill event for the same trade arrives (reorder, reconnect replay, or connector REST-driven OrderFilledEvent). wake() adds ws_pending[trade_id] = now, and nothing ever pops it. After 120 s with history complete, summary.history.lag_s reads 119.0 and keeps growing, so the operator sees a false history lag indefinitely. The AC-09 test's own wake({'type':'trade','trade_id':'999'}) leaves such a phantom entry.
verifier_residual: A fill event of another trading pair on the same connector produces the same permanent false lag and also blocks baseline audits forever. So does a restart replay of a trade older than the 5000-row committed cache and the scan overlap. The finding's second remedy (expiry after a covering complete walk) was applied only to client-id labels.
verifier_evidence: Checked at HEAD 203e31370. engine.py:678-681 (`wake`) skips trade ids already in `_committed_trade_ids`. engine.py:1428-1431 expires client-id-only labels after a complete walk that started after them. engine.py:1471-1478 pops labels on commit. Test test_ng_engine_review1.py::test_r12_ws_signal_for_an_already_committed_trade_is_not_history_lag passes, and both runtime mutations (no committed check; no cid-label expiry) make it fail. Trade-id labels, however, never expire unless this engine commits that row. executor.py:358-364 forwards every connector OrderFilledEvent to `wake` with no trading-pair filter (ExecutorBase registers listeners for the whole connector). Probe scratchpad/verify/test_probe_d107.py sends one trade-id signal that this engine never commits, like another pair's fill: after 120 ticks with history_complete=True, history_lag_s = 120.0 and snapshot lag_s = 119.0, both still growing. `_audit_evidence_unsettled` also refuses baseline audits permanently ('1 WS trade signal(s) not yet in committed history').

title: A cancel that was committed but never sent is never sent during a STOP drain, so the order stays live after stop
requirement: NG-OPS-003 / AC-36 (stop cancels own active orders), NG-DB-002/003 (a PENDING outbox row proves the request was never sent and must be resumed after restart)
original_scenario: During a STOP drain the process dies, or mark_dispatching raises PersistenceError, after record_cancel_intent commits (leg CANCEL_PENDING, CANCEL outbox PENDING) and before mark_dispatching. After restart meta.stop_requested_ms is still set, so _act takes the stop branch. That branch picks only legs in CANCELLABLE={LIVE} or with _cancel_retry_due (CANCEL_UNKNOWN only), then returns without calling _resume_pending_intents. That method (lines 1919-1922) is the only code that dispatches PENDING cancel rows. The leg stays CANCEL_PENDING forever, and _reconcile_active never changes it (it is seen active and is not SUBMIT/TERMINAL_UNKNOWN). The order keeps resting on the venue and can fill after the stop (new exposure after stop). The engine sits in STOP_UNCERTAIN indefinitely, and the launcher detaches after 90 s. The tp_blockers branch (1654-1661) has the same gap: e.g. while FROZEN, a PENDING OUTSIDE_BOUNDS or router cancel is never sent.
verifier_residual: The tp_blockers branch named in the finding is fixed in code, and so is the normal path, because resuming a PENDING cancel moved out of _resume_pending_intents. No committed test pins either path, so a regression there would leave a committed-but-unsent cancel resting on the venue outside a STOP. The blocked branch also waits for startup_reconciled after a restart.
verifier_evidence: Stop branch: engine.py:2144-2150 now adds legs in CANCEL_PENDING that still have a PENDING CANCEL outbox row (_pending_cancel_outbox, line 2120). store.record_cancel_intent returns the open row (store.py:2916-2919), and mark_dispatching then works without a resend. This is pinned by test_ng_engine_review1.py::test_r07_stop_drain_dispatches_a_committed_but_unsent_cancel (line 351, crash at after_cancel_intent_commit). The test passes. Reverting the stop-branch clause makes it fail with 'condition not reached in 60 ticks; state=STOPPING'. Non-stop branches: _risk_reducing_cancels (engine.py:2134-2135, RESUME_PENDING_CANCEL) is used by both the tp_blockers branch (2153-2158, only when startup_reconciled and no PERSISTENCE_FAILURE) and the normal path (2159). My scratch probes pass at HEAD for both: an outside-bounds cancel crashed after its intent commit, in normal state and under a MARKET_NOT_TRADABLE TP blocker, is dispatched and the venue order is gone. However, the mutation that removes the RESUME_PENDING_CANCEL clause survives all 171 tests in test_ng_engine_crash/review1/review2/cycles/ops/risk. Under that mutation both of my probes fail and the order stays open.

title: The LEDGER_INVARIANT freeze set on a store or ledger refusal is dropped by the next tick's reload
requirement: NG-OPS-001 / NG-RISK-004 (unknown or invariant-violating state blocks exposure until audited); trace decision 2 says mismatches surface as LEDGER_INVARIANT freezes that are cleared only by ack_history_conflict (line 1009)
original_scenario: tick() catches StoreError or LedgerError, sets meta.freezes[LEDGER_INVARIANT] only in memory and sets reload_needed. The tick aborted before _commit_snapshot, so engine_meta is never persisted. At the start of the next tick _reload() → _load() re-reads engine_meta from engine_kv, and the freeze disappears. The engine returns to NORMAL with no operator ack; the only trace is the in-memory errors deque.
verifier_residual: If the process dies or restarts within the roughly one-tick window after a store or ledger refusal, the LEDGER_INVARIANT freeze disappears without an operator ack. The engine can return to NORMAL unless the refusal recurs deterministically. The suggested alternative, persisting the freeze in its own transaction inside the handler, would close this window.
verifier_evidence: engine.py:737-744: the StoreError/LedgerError handler now also records FREEZE_INVARIANT in _sticky_freezes. _reload (engine.py:544-560) re-applies it and persists engine_meta in its own transaction. Only ack_history_conflict removes it (engine.py:1221-1227). test_r16_ledger_invariant_freeze_survives_reload_and_restart_until_acknowledged (review1:544) passes, and removing the sticky line makes it fail at line 557. The original scenario (the next tick's reload drops the freeze) is fixed. My scratch probe test_probe_d116_freeze_after_immediate_crash_restart covers a remaining gap. It triggers the refusal, then calls crash_restart() before any further tick. The freeze is lost: the output was 'freezes after immediate crash: {} EngineState.NORMAL'. The freeze is persisted only by the next tick's _reload, never in the except handler.

title: Cells are released using the previous tick's position_reconciled flag, computed before this tick's history commit
requirement: NG-CELL-001 (5): account position and ledger must be reconciled at release time
original_scenario: The tick order is _scan_history → _reconcile_active → _settle → _detect_drift. _settle calls can_release(self.position_reconciled) with the value computed last tick. Suppose this tick's history batch commits an unmatched manual trade (a new store entry blocker) or fills that change P. A cell whose TP settlement completes in the same tick is still released as 'NG-CELL-001 release proven'. _detect_drift then sets position_reconciled=False only afterwards (1440-1443, 1458).
verifier_residual: The fix is correct in code, but the exact mechanism the finding names (release on the previous tick's flag) is not pinned. Neither is the unmatched-manual-trade variant, nor a re-read skipped by the weight budget. A regression in _settle alone would pass the committed suite and allow a premature NG-CELL-001 release.
verifier_evidence: engine.py:1726-1728: _settle now recomputes reconciliation through _position_reconciled_now (engine.py:1377-1382). That requires a fresh position requested after the latest fill commit (position_seq > fills_commit_seq), equality with the ledger P, and no store_entry_blockers. _reread_position_for_release (engine.py:1384-1395, called at line 724 after _scan_history) re-reads the position when a cell waits only on condition (5). test_r17_release_needs_a_position_read_after_the_closing_fill_commit (review1:251) and test_r03 (review1:208) pass. r17 fails only when both parts are reverted (the settle recompute and the re-read): (6, 6, Decimal('0')). Reverting only the _settle line the finding names, so that it uses the previous tick's position_reconciled flag, survives all 115 tests in review1/review2/cycles/ops/risk/history. My scratch probe test_probe_d117_unmatched_manual_trade_in_release_tick_blocks_release covers the manual-trade variant from the finding. An unmatched manual trade executes after the account read and is committed by the same tick's history walk. At HEAD there is no release, blocked by 'unmatched account trade(s)'. Under the _settle-only revert, the cell is released in exactly that tick.

title: Executor STOP is silently lost when its command row becomes CONFLICT, and it is never re-sent
requirement: NG-OPS-003, AC-35, AC-36, NG-UI-003 (Stop follows NG-OPS-003, honest outcome)
original_scenario: The operator clicks Pause in the web UI, or any other command is applied, or the engine state changes (set_engine_state bumps engine_revision) while a tick is suspended on an await. Then Hummingbot `stop` runs: the launcher's on_stop calls drain_neutral_executors, which calls executor.early_stop(). That enqueues STOP with the revision current at that moment. At the next tick, claim_next_command turns the STOP into CONFLICT/stale_at_apply. early_stop has already set _stop_command_sent=True and never checks or re-enqueues; re-enqueueing with the same pid key returns the same CONFLICT row. The engine keeps running (PAUSED/NORMAL) and never cancels its orders. After 90 s the drain calls executor.stop(), which closes the store. The connector's cancel_all skips the engine-owned CIDs, so every owned order stays live on the venue. meta.stop_requested_ms is None, so no STOP_UNCERTAIN is recorded, and the log line wrongly claims 'durable state (STOP_UNCERTAIN) will be reconciled on the next start'. On restart the engine resumes normal trading.
verifier_residual: If the STOP insert fails once (SQLITE_BUSY from the web command client past its 5 s busy timeout, disk full, or an I/O error), the Hummingbot stop is lost for good. The engine keeps trading. The drain times out as STOP_NOT_APPLIED, but its log still says orders are 'reconciled on the next start', and the next launcher START resumes normal trading. Suggested fix: re-send when the tracked key has no row, or enqueue before recording the key and retry on exception.
verifier_evidence: Fix: executor.py:250-271 (_track_stop re-sends STOP with a new key and fresh revisions on CONFLICT/REJECTED; _stop_command_sent is set only when APPLIED). scripts/lighter_robinhood_fixed_neutral_grid.py:50 and 216-255: the drain now waits stop_uncertain_after_s+30 = 150 s and reports the committed outcome (STOP_NOT_APPLIED / STOPPING / the committed outcome). Test test/controllers/generic/test_neutral_grid.py::test_a_hummingbot_stop_is_resent_after_a_conflict_until_the_engine_applies_it passes. A mutation that restores the old no-re-send behaviour makes it fail (no APPLIED stop row). The CONFLICT scenario is fixed and pinned. Variant still reachable: _send_stop records the key before enqueue (268-271), and _track_stop treats a missing row (record None, 258-260) the same as QUEUED. Probe scratchpad/verify/probe_d201.py forced one failed STOP insert (FaultHooks.fail_statement('INSERT INTO commands', OperationalError('database is locked'))). early_stop then raised PersistenceError, which would also raise out of orchestrator.execute_actions in the drain. For the next 200 ticks the engine stayed NORMAL with 10 owned orders live, there was no STOP row, and the STOP was never re-sent. stop_requested_ms stayed None.

title: LEDGER_INVARIANT freeze is not durable: it is wiped by _reload on the next tick, and the FROZEN state is never committed
requirement: NG-DB-003 step 7 (stay paused on any ambiguity), NG-UI-002 / §11 honest committed state
original_scenario: Any StoreError or LedgerError inside a tick (a store/ledger projection mismatch, such as close_cycle refused by B while A says can_release, or a refused leg transition) sets meta.freezes['LEDGER_INVARIANT'] only in memory, plus reload_needed=True, and skips _commit_snapshot. On the next tick _reload() calls _load(), which replaces self.meta from the committed engine_meta. The freeze disappears and the engine evaluates NORMAL and dispatches entries again without any operator ack, even though ack_history_conflict exists specifically to clear FREEZE_INVARIANT. If the error recurs every tick, no snapshot is ever committed, so UI and CLI keep showing the last (possibly NORMAL) committed state.
verifier_residual: The second half of the finding is still reachable: while the refusal recurs every tick, no FROZEN state or snapshot is ever committed (no set_engine_state in the except or _reload path). Web and CLI keep showing the last committed NORMAL state.
verifier_evidence: engine.py:733-744: the except path records the LEDGER_INVARIANT freeze in _sticky_freezes. _reload (544-560) re-applies it and persists engine_meta. Only ack_history_conflict clears it (1234-1236). Test test_ng_engine_review1.py::test_r16_ledger_invariant_freeze_survives_reload_and_restart_until_acknowledged passes, and fails when the mutation clears the sticky freezes before reload. Probe scratchpad/verify/probe_d204.py made _reconcile_active raise StoreError on every tick. The freeze is now kept in memory (FROZEN) and in durable engine_meta, and no entries are sent (0 submits). However: committed engine row engine_state=NORMAL, committed snapshot engine_state=NORMAL, and format_status prints 'state NORMAL' with no reason. Only a SNAPSHOT STALE tag appears after 15 s. The health sidecar covers only persistence/fatal errors.

title: Baseline audit rebases on a position read that may predate the last committed history batch
requirement: NG-RISK-003 / AC-30 (the audit must not change obligations or mask fills); NG-RISK-001 (baseline exactness)
original_scenario: Account poll at t=100 (every 5 s). A LIVE entry fills 10 at t=101. A WS wake causes a scan that commits the fill at t=102, so ledger buys include +10. The operator's baseline audit is applied at t=103 with observed_position equal to position(t=100). new_baseline = venue - buys + sells understates B by 10, and the rebase is persisted in the audit trail. The next poll shows venue != P, so drift or POSITION_UNRECONCILED blocks again and another audit is required. The audit mis-rebases a known fill instead of refusing a stale comparison.
verifier_residual: The code path is fixed, but no test pins the finding's scenario (position read older than a committed fill). test_d covers only the reverse case, where history lags the position. Reverting line 1059 would go unnoticed.
verifier_evidence: engine.py:1056-1070 (line 1059): _audit_evidence_unsettled refuses the audit (AUDIT_EVIDENCE_NOT_SETTLED, retryable) when position_seq < fills_commit_seq, which is the suggested fix. It also refuses on history lag, pending WS signals, no complete walk after the position read, or unresolved orders. Probe scratchpad/verify/probe_d207.py ran the exact scenario: account poll, then a 4 LIT own fill committed before the next poll, then an audit with observed=7. Current code: REJECTED, reason 'position read predates the latest committed fill'. With that single check neutralised, the audit is APPLIED with new_effective_baseline 3 instead of 7. Under the same mutation, test_ng_engine_risk.py, test_ng_engine_review1.py and test_ng_engine_review2.py (74 tests, including test_d_baseline_audit_is_refused_while_an_own_fill_may_be_missing_from_history and test_r13) all still pass.

title: resolve_unknown_submit accepts 'not landed' on an active list and history walk from before the dispatch, so a new CID goes out while the original order is live
requirement: NG-HIST-001, NG-DB-005, AC-56, AC-16/17 (handoff: active-list absence is not proof; no new CID after a timeout)
original_scenario: A submit times out (TransportOutcome.UNKNOWN) but lands on the venue, and the venue's active list lags by a few seconds. About 2 s later the operator sends baseline_audit {action: resolve_unknown_submit, cid}. The engine checks self.history_complete, which is true from a walk that finished before the dispatch. It then checks that the CID is absent from self.active_rows, which was fetched before the dispatch (or is None after a failed poll, which passes as an empty list). It does not check freshness, a walk started after intent_ms, or the settlement delay. The leg becomes REJECTED_ZERO_FILL, _retry_only() allows a new revision, and a second 10 LIT BUY with a new CID is placed for the same cell. Only on a later poll is the old order seen 'final but still active' (RISK_BLOCKED). By then the cell has double exposure.
verifier_residual: Venue active-list or history lag of a few seconds still lets an audited 'not landed' through, producing a new CID and double exposure for the cell. Needs settlement delay plus N walks started after dispatch+delay, and no pending WS signal, before accepting.
verifier_evidence: engine.py:1256-1271 resolve_unknown_submit now calls _absence_not_proven (engine.py:1274-1290). It requires an active list requested after the outbox dispatched_at_ms and within history_freshness_s, plus one complete walk that started after the dispatch. review1::test_r08_resolve_unknown_submit_is_refused_without_an_active_list and ::test_r08_..._with_an_active_list_older_than_the_dispatch pin the stale and None cases, and both pass. The suggested settlement predicate was not implemented: no settlement_delay_s, no settlement_scans, no check for a pending WS signal on that CID. Probe scratchpad/verify/test_probe_d15.py: FakeExchange(active_lag_s=7), TP with TIMEOUT_LANDED, operator retries resolve_unknown_submit each tick. It is REJECTED at +1..+5 s and APPLIED at +6 s while the venue order is still open. Leg -> REJECTED_ZERO_FILL, a second TP CID for the same cell goes out (two open TP orders at the venue), and the state is NORMAL until it later turns RISK_BLOCKED 'final order ... is still active on the venue'. title: A CID collision latches FREEZE_CID forever and blocks every TP; no audited recovery path exists
requirement: NG-RISK-003 (manual orders must not drop TP obligations), NG-OPS-001, AC-43 (fail closed without dead-locking obligations)
original_scenario: A manual or foreign order on the account uses the client id that the store would allocate next. It is seen in active orders and recorded in foreign_cids. The next TP intent raises CidCollisionError, and the engine sets meta.freezes['CID_ALLOCATION']. That freeze is in _FREEZES_BLOCKING_TP, so no TP obligation of any cell is dispatched again. Nothing clears it: AUDIT_ACTIONS has no action for it, _cmd_reconcile never pops FREEZE_CID, and store.retire_cid (the recovery the store documents) is never called by the engine. Exits stay blocked until the operator edits the SQLite engine_kv by hand.
verifier_residual: In a real deployment an operator still cannot clear FREEZE_CID, which blocks every TP, without hand-writing a command row into the SQLite queue (store.enqueue_command from Python). That is audited now, unlike the old engine_kv edit, but there is still no operator path.
verifier_evidence: The engine now remembers meta.colliding_cid (sticky across reload) at engine.py:2369-2375. The audited action 'retire_colliding_cid' (engine.py:1239-1248) calls store.retire_cid and pops FREEZE_CID in the command transaction. review2::test_f_cid_collision_is_recovered_by_an_audited_retire passes and would fail without the action. The action is in commands.EXTENDED_AUDIT_ACTIONS only, and no product surface can send it: web/neutral_grid/commands.py:37-40,218 accepts only the base AUDIT_ACTIONS ('Недопустимое действие аудита' otherwise), and git grep finds no launcher, bin or controller code that enqueues retire_colliding_cid. The trace itself leaves this as open request R5. The suggested automatic retire of an id already recorded as foreign was not implemented.

title: The baseline audit (AC-30 rebase) absorbs an own fill that history has not delivered yet into the baseline, then counts it twice
requirement: NG-RISK-003 / AC-30 (the rebase must not hide unknown fills), NG-RISK-001/002 (P = B + buys - sells)
original_scenario: A manual BUY of 7 causes drift, and entries are blocked pending audit. While the venue's history lags, a grid entry partially fills 4. The position shows 11 at once; the trade is not yet in history. The engine has a pending WS trade signal (history_lag_s = 6 s) and venue != P. The audit is still accepted because history is 'complete and fresh', the position is fresh, and the filled entry is still LIVE, so it is not 'unresolved'. new_baseline = 11 - 0 + 0 = 11 instead of 7. When the fill reaches history, the ledger gives P = 15 against a venue position of 11. The engine reports NORMAL for the next 30 s (position_gap_grace_s), then POSITION_UNRECONCILED, and it needs a second audit. The durable audit trail records a wrong effective baseline.
verifier_residual: A missed or dropped WS event (the spec treats WS as a hint only) still lets the rebase absorb an own fill into B and count it twice. Needs a check that no owned LIVE order's active-row cumulative filled exceeds its history-proven fills (or a settlement delay after the position read).
verifier_evidence: engine.py:1028-1033 and 1056-1070: the audit is refused with AUDIT_EVIDENCE_NOT_SETTLED when the position was read before the latest fill commit, when any WS signal is pending or history lag > 0, when no complete walk started after the position read, or when non-LIVE own orders exist. review2::test_d_baseline_audit_is_refused_while_an_own_fill_may_be_missing_from_history (lagging fill with WS signal) passes. Probe scratchpad/verify/test_probe_d18.py reproduces the finding's case with a WS signal: REJECTED. Probe scratchpad/verify/test_probe_d18b.py uses the same scenario, but the own fill arrives without a WS event (fx.fill(..., history_lag_s=30, ws=False)), the only difference. The audit is APPLIED at +9 s with new_effective_baseline=11. After history delivers the fill, P=15 vs venue 11 and the state is still NORMAL. The owned LIVE entry's active row already reported filled_base_amount=4 (recorded as order evidence in _reconcile_active), but _audit_evidence_unsettled does not compare active-row cumulative with ledger fills.

title: Lighter auth token reaches the committed snapshot, /api/state, the web UI and CLI status through the ACTIVE_ORDERS_UNAVAILABLE error text
requirement: Handoff/spec forbid secrets in logs, API or UI. Spec §11: "Секреты и auth token не выводятся". NG-UI-001 forbids secrets in API responses. NG-UI-002 says the drill-down and audit history must contain no secrets.
original_scenario:
1. LighterAuth.rest_authenticate (lighter_perpetual_auth.py:26) always adds `auth=<token>` to the query of authenticated GETs. fetch_active_orders (lighter_perpetual_derivative.py, is_auth_required=True) is one of them.
2. Lighter or a proxy/CDN answers accountActiveOrders with a status below 400 and a Content-Type that is not JSON, text/plain or text/html. Examples: an empty 200/204 with no Content-Type (aiohttp reports it as application/octet-stream), or text/xml.
3. Hummingbot's RESTResponse.json() then calls aiohttp's json(), which raises aiohttp.ContentTypeError. Its str() is `200, message='Attempt to decode JSON ...', url='https://.../accountActiveOrders?account_index=..&market_id=..&auth=<TOKEN>'`.
4. ContentTypeError is not an IOError, so it passes through _api_request unchanged. LighterExchangePort.active_orders (lighter_port.py:348) catches only LighterHistoryResponseError, so it passes through there too.
5. NeutralGridEngine._refresh_account catches it at engine.py:1349-1351: `self._error("ACTIVE_ORDERS_UNAVAILABLE", f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", now)`. No redaction is applied.
6. snapshot.build_summary copies engine.errors into the snapshot (snapshot.py:224). The snapshot is committed to SQLite and served by /api/state (server.py:179 `errors`). app.js renderErrors shows it in the UI. format_status prints the last 5 errors in the CLI `status` (snapshot.py:329-330). executor.get_custom_info also exposes the snapshot to the V2 controller.
The token grants read access to the account's private orders and trades for about 10 minutes (DEFAULT_AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRY_SECONDS). The copy in the SQLite snapshot rows is persisted indefinitely.
Other history paths only record type(exc).__name__: the scanner's page_fetch_error and the port's submit/cancel. This active-orders path is the gap.
verifier_evidence:
Reproduced offline with scratch test /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mikhail/ed31a3df-55bd-475b-8111-912d06f80d1d/scratchpad/verify/test_scratch_auth_leak.py (2 passed).
(a) LighterExchangePort(stub).active_orders() re-raises the aiohttp.ContentTypeError, and its str() contains `auth=SECRET_LIGHTER_AUTH_TOKEN_abc123`.
(b) With the real engine harness, fx.active_orders was patched to raise that exception and the engine ran 3 ticks. engine.latest_committed_snapshot()['errors'] then contained `ContentTypeError: 200, message='Attempt to decode JSON with unexpected mimetype: application/octet-stream', url='https://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/api/v1/accountActiveOrders?account_index=4242&market_id=5&auth=SECRET_LIGHTER_AUTH_TOKEN_abc123'`.
Code: engine.py:1346-1351 (`except Exception as exc: ... self._error("ACTIVE_ORDERS_UNAVAILABLE", f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", now)`); lighter_port.py:348-352 (only LighterHistoryResponseError is wrapped); lighter_perpetual_auth.py:24-26 (`params.setdefault("auth", auth_token)`); server.py:179; snapshot.py:224 and 329-330.
No redaction: security.redact_text exists but is never applied to engine errors.

title: Scoped TP freeze misses scanner-withheld conflicts: a cell whose committed fill is contradicted still gets a new TP from that quantity
requirement: NG-HIST-002 / AC-40: one key with a different payload is a history conflict and pauses; quantity is never guessed. NG-OPS-001: an unknown fill blocks new exposure of the affected cell. The review fix #2 (trace ws-d-engine.md row 2) limits TP blocking to the affected cells via `tp_blocked_cells`.
original_scenario: Two review fixes combine badly. (1) The history scanner now withholds conflicted keys (history.py:658-667), so the store never records them. (2) `_scoped_tp_blocks` only blocks TPs for cells named by a store `open_conflicts` row with a CID. A payload or committed-payload conflict on an own trade therefore never names its cell. Walk-through: entry fill T1=3 is committed, and the TP is held below the 5 LIT floor. The venue then re-serves T1 with size 1, which is a `committed_payload_mismatch`. The engine goes FROZEN, but `tp_blocked_cells=={}` and there are no store conflicts. A further fill of 2 makes the committed E=5, and a TP of 5 is dispatched and goes LIVE. That TP is built from the contradicted 3. If the venue's corrected value is true, the TP over-closes the cell by 2 LIT and creates unintended net exposure, while the engine reports FROZEN. The store headroom check does not help because it uses the committed E=5.
verifier_evidence: Scratch probe /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mikhail/ed31a3df-55bd-475b-8111-912d06f80d1d/scratchpad/verify/test_probe_ack_conflict.py::test_probe_tp_dispatched_for_cell_with_contradicted_fill prints: `after conflict: EngineState.FROZEN [... 'STORE:manual reconciliation required: history conflict: conflict:committed_payload_mismatch:...']`, `tp_blocked_cells: {} open store conflicts: []`, `E: 5 TPs: [(1099511627787, '5', 'LIVE')] state: EngineState.FROZEN`, `cell blocker: None`. `_scoped_tp_blocks` (engine.py:1928-1941) iterates only `self.open_conflicts` (store rows). `_apply_history` (engine.py ~1580) turns scanner conflicts only into `mark_manual_reconcile_required`, with no cell or CID mapping, even though the withheld row carries `own_client_order_id`.

title: Operator ack_history_conflict cannot restore history completeness for payload conflicts; the grid stays RECONCILING forever and STOP ends STOP_UNCERTAIN
requirement: NG-HIST-002 / AC-40 / AC-12: a conflict pauses until an operator audit. The web offers `ack_history_conflict` as that audit, and `_acknowledge_scan_conflicts` documents that audited conflicts 'are not re-flagged, and the walk boundary is rebased'. NG-OPS-003: stop must be able to finish once own orders are terminal.
original_scenario: The venue keeps serving an own trade or order row whose payload differs from the committed one, e.g. a changed field (`committed_payload_mismatch`) or a duplicate with another payload. The operator audits it with `ack_history_conflict`, which is APPLIED. `_only_audited_conflicts` converts a walk to complete only when every conflict starts with `conflict:trades_exceed_order_cumulative:`, so every later walk stays `complete=False` / `conflict`. Rebasing the floor to now-overlap does not help. `_fetch_page` (history.py:602-605) applies every row of a page, including rows older than the boundary, so the contradicted row keeps conflicting while it is within the first 100 rows. On a low-volume grid that is indefinitely. The results: history_complete stays False, so no leg settles and no cell releases; entries stay blocked with HISTORY_INCOMPLETE; a venue-cancelled partially filled entry stays TERMINAL_UNKNOWN; a STOP can only end STOP_UNCERTAIN. No other audit action lifts this.
verifier_evidence: Probe test_probe_ack_conflict.py::test_probe_committed_payload_mismatch_after_ack (same scratch dir). After an APPLIED ack (`{'status': 'APPLIED', 'result': {'resolved_conflicts': []}}`) and 600 ticks it prints `last: (599, 'RECONCILING', False, 'conflict')` and `walk conflicts: ['conflict:committed_payload_mismatch:...']`. After a venue cancel it prints `entry after venue cancel: TERMINAL_UNKNOWN 2 history_complete False`, and after STOP `stop outcome: STOP_UNCERTAIN`. The sibling probe test_probe_persistent_payload_conflict_after_ack shows the same for `duplicate_key_payload_mismatch`. Code: engine.py:1449-1465 (kind whitelist), engine.py:1072-1082 (ack only rebases the floor), history.py:602-615.

title: Launcher START that turns CONFLICT is silently dropped; an explicit resume-after-stop phrase has no effect
requirement: Review fix A/B and NG-OPS-003 / AC-36: a durable stop may be resumed only by an explicit operator START or a launcher resume naming that stop. Operator commands must reflect committed state, and a refused start must be visible (`start_error`).
original_scenario: The executor enqueues the launcher START (with `resume_stop_ms`) in `on_start` using the current revisions. An older queued command, for example a PAUSE clicked in the attach-mode web UI while Hummingbot was down, is claimed first in the same tick and APPLIED, which bumps `engine_revision`. `claim_next_command` then marks the launcher START as CONFLICT (`stale_at_apply`). `_track_start` only reacts to REJECTED. Review fix A made `_track_stop` re-send a CONFLICTed STOP, and `_maybe_migrate` / `_maybe_confirm_baseline` retry too, but START was not given the same handling. The START is never re-sent and `start_error` stays None, so the engine silently stays STOPPED although the operator typed the exact resume phrase for that stop.
verifier_evidence: Probe /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mikhail/ed31a3df-55bd-475b-8111-912d06f80d1d/scratchpad/verify/test_probe_launcher_start.py::test_probe_resume_start_lost_when_older_command_applies_first prints `('start', 'CONFLICT', 'launcher-start-...', {... 'reason': 'stale_at_apply'})`, `('pause', 'APPLIED', 'web-pause-000000000001', ...)`, `state: EngineState.STOPPED stop_requested_ms: 1790000025000 outcome: STOPPED`, `start_error: None start_refused: False`. Code: executor.py:273-283 checks only `record.status == CommandStatus.REJECTED`; store.py:3953-3956 converts stale rows to CONFLICT at claim.

title: Executor forwards every connector fill as a WS trade hint; fills outside this market never clear, so lag grows forever and baseline audits are refused
requirement: AC-13: history lag must be shown honestly. AC-30 / NG-RISK-003: a baseline audit or rebase must stay possible. Review fix D refuses the audit while any WS trade signal is pending.
original_scenario: ExecutorBase registers the fill forwarder on the whole connector, so `process_order_filled_event` fires for every order of that connector. `_wake` forwards each one without checking `event.trading_pair` or whether `event.order_id` is a grid CID. `engine.wake` stores the trade id in `ws_pending`, and it is removed only when that trade id is committed from this market's history. Trade labels are never pruned by complete walks. Any fill of another market on the same connector therefore stays pending forever, for example another V2 controller using this generic controller's connector. `history_lag_s` then grows without bound (a false AC-13 lag in snapshot, UI and CLI). `_audit_evidence_unsettled` (engine.py:1061) makes every `baseline` audit REJECTED with `AUDIT_EVIDENCE_NOT_SETTLED`, so after drift the operator can never rebase.
verifier_evidence: Probe test_probe_ack_conflict.py::test_probe_foreign_ws_fill_blocks_baseline_audit_forever (engine.wake with a trade id that never appears in this market's history) prints `lag: 300.0 ws_pending: {'777000111': ...}`, `audit: REJECTED {'error': 'AUDIT_EVIDENCE_NOT_SETTLED', 'reasons': ['1 WS trade signal(s) not yet in committed history', 'history lag 300.0 s'], 'retryable': True}`, `snapshot lag: 301.0`. Code: executor.py:357-365 has no filter; engine.py:665-684 is `ws_pending.setdefault`; engine.py:1437-1438 prunes only non-trade labels; executor_base.py:59/329-335 subscribes on the whole connector.

title: Launcher pre-start ledger reads fail on an older schema: the resume phrase is ignored and CID pre-registration is skipped
requirement: Review fix B/E: the launcher reads the durable stop and registers engine-owned CIDs before the connector's polling starts. Schema migration must be fail-closed but must not disable operator confirmations.
original_scenario: `register_durable_cids` and `durable_stop_ms` use `NeutralGridStore.open_readonly`, which refuses any database older than the code's latest migration (`allow_upgrade=False`). The v3 `m0003_drilldown_indexes` was added late, so a ledger created by an earlier build is v2. On the first launch after upgrading, both reads raise SchemaVersionError. The launcher's broad except logs it and continues with `stop_ms=None`: no resume notice is shown, the operator's `resume_after_stop_confirmation` is ignored (so the engine then REJECTS the START with DURABLE_STOP_ACTIVE), and no durable CIDs are registered before polling. Only a second restart, after the executor has upgraded the DB, behaves as documented.
verifier_evidence: Probe /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mikhail/ed31a3df-55bd-475b-8111-912d06f80d1d/scratchpad/verify/test_probe_old_schema.py creates the DB with MIGRATIONS[:-1] and prints `raised: SchemaVersionError database schema 2 is older than 3; the engine must migrate it first` for both `durable_stop_ms` and `register_durable_cids`. Code: scripts/lighter_robinhood_fixed_neutral_grid.py:170-181 (except Exception -> stop_ms stays None); executor.py durable_stop_ms/register_durable_cids -> store.py:1587-1588.

title: Example config documents the wrong default ledger path after review fix E
requirement: NG-DB-004 / AC-54: operators must restore the correct database from backup. Review fix E changed the default ledger to the store's per-account/market path.
original_scenario: The example says `default is <hummingbot data path>/neutral_grid_<grid_id>.sqlite`. With `db_path: null` the code actually uses `default_db_path(identity)` = `<data>/neutral_grid/neutral_grid.<domain>.<account>.<pair>.sqlite3`, as `engine_db_path` in executor.py and `NeutralGridStore.open(None, ...)` do. An operator backing up, restoring or pointing `--attach-db` at the documented file uses a path that never exists. After a loss, the host marker then makes the engine fail closed (PriorRunEvidenceError) while the real ledger sits elsewhere.
